reuse.why: The change uses recurConfigToRSchedule and applyWeekendRule, but repeats occurrence eligibility decisions across consumers and replaces delegation to getDateWithSkippedWeekend with overlapping adjustment logic.

duplication.why: Daily eligibility filtering is repeated across handlers and getNextDate, getNextDate repeats its own filter, and two weekend adjustment implementations remain.

placement.why: The handler and configuration additions belong in their existing modules, but shared scheduling policy is also implemented directly in server handlers.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration plumbing, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several eligibility implementations, two holiday matching expressions, and overlapping weekend adjustment helpers when extending the scheduling policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange implement daily eligibility locally, while applyWeekendRule stops delegating weekend movement to the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend helper.

disguised_duplication.where: The server handlers express the daily eligibility decision as an inline disjunction with holidays.includes, while getNextDate expresses it through shouldSkipDailyWeekend and isHoliday; these reshape the same policy rather than share it.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains holidays; getNextDate adds a daily-specific take selection and two conditional filtering blocks; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange decide eligibility locally, while createScheduleList continues using raw occurrences plus adjustment instead of the daily eligibility decision.
